## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(plotly)
library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
library(mdsr)
library(sf)
library(ggspatial)
library(leaflet)
library(tidyverse)
```


When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}

#Reading Data
full_data <- read_csv("../data/combined_data.csv")

# Create sf object for US counties
states_map <- maps::map("state", region = ".",
                       plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE)|>  st_as_sf()

#Hard coded vector for states
state_names <- c(
  "AL" = "Alabama", "AZ" = "Arizona", "AR" = "Arkansas", "CA" = "California", 
  "CO" = "Colorado", "CT" = "Connecticut", "DE" = "Delaware", 
  "DC" = "District of Columbia", "FL" = "Florida", "GA" = "Georgia", 
  "ID" = "Idaho", "IL" = "Illinois", "IN" = "Indiana", "IA" = "Iowa", 
  "KS" = "Kansas", "KY" = "Kentucky", "LA" = "Louisiana", "ME" = "Maine",
  "MD" = "Maryland", "MA" = "Massachusetts", "MI" = "Michigan", 
  "MN" = "Minnesota", "MS" = "Mississippi", "MO" = "Missouri",
  "MT" = "Montana", "NE" = "Nebraska", "NV" = "Nevada",
  "NH" = "New Hampshire", "NJ" = "New Jersey", "NM" = "New Mexico",
  "NY" = "New York", "NC" = "North Carolina", "ND" = "North Dakota",
  "OH" = "Ohio", "OK" = "Oklahoma", "OR" = "Oregon", "PA" = "Pennsylvania", 
  "RI" = "Rhode Island", "SC" = "South Carolina", "SD" = "South Dakota",
  "TN" = "Tennessee", "TX" = "Texas", "UT" = "Utah", "VT" = "Vermont", 
  "VA" = "Virginia", "WA" = "Washington", "WV" = "West Virginia", 
  "WI" = "Wisconsin", "WY" = "Wyoming"
)

#Recode state names in full_data from initials to full names
full_data <- full_data |>
  mutate(State = recode(State, !!!state_names))

#Recode and leftjoin to create dataset with the location
states_map <- states_map |>
  mutate(State = stringr::str_to_title(ID)) |> 
  select(-ID)

full_data_with_state <- left_join(states_map, full_data, by = "State")

#All unique months (chronologically) and filter which one we want
unique_months <- sort(unique(full_data_with_state$month))
month_variable = unique_months[1]
month_name <- format(as.Date(month_variable), "%B %Y")
full_data_with_state_specific_month <- full_data_with_state |> 
  filter(month == month_variable)

#Create a plot for the specific month
Gasplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_specific_month, 
                  aes(geometry = geom, fill = MRA_Regular,
                      #This change hover label
                      text = paste0(
                        "State: ", State,
                        "<br>Gas Price: $", round(MRA_Regular, 3)))) +
  geom_sf() +
  scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", direction = 1) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = paste("Average Regular Gas Price by State,"),
    subtitle = "Real (inflation-adjusted) prices per gallon",
    fill = "Price ($/gal)",
    caption = paste("Month:", month_name))

plotly::ggplotly(Gasplot, tooltip = "text")


```



You can add options to executable code like this 


```{r}
#Creating the slider map

# Creating scale for every month so shades are comparable across months
price_limits <- range(full_data_with_state$MRA_Regular, na.rm = TRUE)

# Empty list to then fill with the plots
month_plots <- list()
# For loop to create a different month in each index
for (i in seq_along(unique_months)) {
  #Filtering for the unique month
  month_variable <- unique_months[i]
  month_name <- format(as.Date(month_variable), "%B %Y")
  full_data_with_state_specific_month <- full_data_with_state |> 
    filter(month == month_variable)
  #Creating plot
  Gasplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_specific_month, 
                    aes(geometry = geom, fill = MRA_Regular,
                        text = paste0(
                          "State: ", State,
                          "<br>Gas Price: $", round(MRA_Regular, 3)))) +
    geom_sf() +
    scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", direction = 1, limits = price_limits) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Average Regular Gas Price by State"),
      subtitle = "Real (inflation-adjusted) prices per gallon",
      fill = "Price ($/gal)",
      caption = paste("Month:", month_name))
  #Add it to month_plots
  month_plots[[i]] <- Gasplot}

# Replicating the list but for plotly instead of ggplot
plotly_plots <- list()
for (i in seq_along(month_plots)) {
  plotly_plots[[i]] <- plotly_build(ggplotly(month_plots[[i]], tooltip = "text"))}

# This part is probably the most confusing, so I had to learn a bit about how
# Plotly works. Each month's plotly plot has its own set of "traces", 
# that together produces the plot. We need to group these traces so that Plotly 
# knows what to display for each month.

# Empty list that will collect the trace from every month
all_traces <- list()
# Empty vector to record which month each trace came from.
trace_month <- c()
# Go through each month's plotly plot, one at a time
for (i in seq_along(plotly_plots)) {
  # Grab this month's traces and appends it
  month_traces <- plotly_plots[[i]]$x$data
  all_traces <- c(all_traces, month_traces)
  # Labels where the trace came from
  trace_month <- c(trace_month, rep(i, length(month_traces)))}

# This for loop is to determine which traces are intially shown (Month 1)
for (j in seq_along(all_traces)) {
  all_traces[[j]]$visible <- trace_month[j] == 1}

# Inherit Month 1's Layout
combined <- plotly_plots[[1]]
# Then add the trace
combined$x$data <- all_traces

# Create the slider and the ticker marks
tickers <- list()
for (i in seq_along(unique_months)) {
  month_name <- format(as.Date(unique_months[i]), "%B %Y")
  show_specific_month <- trace_month == i
  #Controls what occurs on each ticker 
  tickers[[i]] <- list(
    method = "restyle", 
    args = list("visible", show_specific_month), 
    label = month_name)
}

# Attach the slider to the combined figure
combined$x$layout$sliders <- list(
  list(
    active = 0,                                  
    currentvalue = list(prefix = "Month: "), 
    x = 0.1,
    y = 0.2,
    steps = tickers))

combined
```



```{r}
# This is essentially the same as the last map but I'm adding unemployment to 
# to the right of the map for gas prices

# Fixed color scale for each variable, so shades are comparable across months
gas_limits   <- range(full_data_with_state$MRA_Regular, na.rm = TRUE)
unemp_limits <- range(full_data_with_state$unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE)

# Empty list which is then filled with both maps
plotly_plots <- list()
for (i in seq_along(unique_months)) {
  month_variable <- unique_months[i]
  full_data_with_state_specific_month <- full_data_with_state |>
    filter(month == month_variable)
  # Left map: Gas Prices (blue)
  Gasplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_specific_month,
                    aes(geometry = geom, fill = MRA_Regular,
                        text = paste0(
                          "State: ", State,
                          "<br>Gas Price: $", round(MRA_Regular, 3)))) +
    geom_sf() +
    scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", direction = 1, limits = gas_limits) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(fill = "Gas ($/gal)")
  # Right map: Unemployment Rate (red)
  Unempplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_specific_month,
                      aes(geometry = geom, fill = unemployment_rate,
                          text = paste0(
                            "State: ", State,
                            "<br>Unemployment Rate: ",
                            round(unemployment_rate, 2), "%"))) +
    geom_sf() +
    scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", palette = "Reds", direction = 1,
                         limits = unemp_limits) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(fill = "Unemployment (%)")

  # Side-by-side figure for one month
  fig <- plotly_build(
    subplot(
      ggplotly(Gasplot, tooltip = "text"),
      ggplotly(Unempplot, tooltip = "text"),
      nrows = 1, margin = 0.08))
  # Adjusting position of the legends by finding legend from the traces 
  # and then changing x position.
  bar_x <- c(0.42, 1)
  cb <- 0
  for (k in seq_along(fig$x$data)) {
    if (!is.null(fig$x$data[[k]]$marker$colorbar)) {
      cb <- cb + 1
      fig$x$data[[k]]$marker$colorbar$x <- bar_x[cb]
      fig$x$data[[k]]$marker$colorbar$len <- 0.3
      fig$x$data[[k]]$marker$colorbar$lenmode <- "fraction"
    }}
  plotly_plots[[i]] <- fig
}

# Sorting all the traces by month
all_traces  <- list()
trace_month <- c()
for (i in seq_along(plotly_plots)) {
  month_traces <- plotly_plots[[i]]$x$data
  all_traces  <- c(all_traces, month_traces)
  trace_month <- c(trace_month, rep(i, length(month_traces)))}

# Starting view is Month 1
for (j in seq_along(all_traces)) {
  all_traces[[j]]$visible <- trace_month[j] == 1}

# Inherit Month 1's Layout, then add in all traces
combined <- plotly_plots[[1]]
combined$x$data <- all_traces

# One slider step per month
tickers <- list()
for (i in seq_along(unique_months)) {
  month_name <- format(as.Date(unique_months[i]), "%B %Y")
  show_specific_month <- trace_month == i
  tickers[[i]] <- list(
    method = "restyle",
    args = list("visible", show_specific_month),
    label = month_name)}

# Attach the slider
combined$x$layout$sliders <- list(
  list(active = 0,
    currentvalue = list(prefix = "Month: "),
    x = 0.15,
    y = 0.23,
    steps = tickers))

# Centered Titles for the two maps 
combined$x$layout$annotations <- list(
  list(text = "Average Regular Gas \n Price by State", 
       x = 0.21, y = 0.73, 
       xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
       showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "center"),
  list(text = "Unemployment by by State", 
       x = 0.79, y = 0.7, 
       xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
       showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "center"))

combined
```


The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
